newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO STOCKS REVERSE GAINS ON PROFIT-TAKING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO STOCKS REVERSE GAINS ON PROFIT-TAKING.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed their early record rise in late morning trade after dealers stepped in to take profits notched up in recent sessions, traders said.
"What we are seeing is a bit of profit-taking, as in recent sessions, but it may only be intraday as foreign investment is still flowing in," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 28.28 points, or 0.54 percent, at 5,184.61. The IPC had surged to a trading record of 5,272.87 in early trade.
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable in the case of Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which weighs heaviest on the IPC.
Telmex was off 10 centavos at 21.55 pesos, down from an earlier high of 21.90 pesos. The telecomms firm's ADR followed suit by shedding 1/8 to trade at 55-7/16.
Trading volume was moderate at 62.1 million shares traded.
On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 52 to 29, out of 102 stocks traded in total.
